title: TrailRunCoach · race prep for trail running and Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue)
description: Signed up for a trail race? Estimate your finish time, the pace of every leg and your fuelling from your own running data, and get a schedule to get there. For trail running, Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) and road running.

hero.h1: Signed up for a trail race? See whether your training gets you there, and how to run every leg.
hero.lead: Race prep for trail running, Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) and road running: race estimates, a schedule and plain-language reading of every run, from your own running data.
cta.price: Free for now, with limited places; when full, you join the waitlist.
shot.fictional: Screens show demo data: a fictional runner and fictional races.
shot.race_alt: The race calculator's estimate: finish time, average power, pace and effort
points.label: Three things
points.terrain.p: Climbs, descents, pack weight, race-day temperature and altitude all become a pace you can actually run.
points.plan.h: A schedule that follows your races and your form
points.plan.p: Phases from your target races, weeks laid out your way; replanned when things change, and big changes are asked first.
points.sources.p: Every method cites public literature; a number without one is marked "estimate" and calibrated on your data.
race.lead: Drop in a course GPX and get the finish time and, for every leg, pace, power, a heart-rate cap and how much to eat and drink.
race.li.legs: Leg by leg: where to run, where walking is faster, where steep descents are about safety
race.li.weather: Race-day weather: heat load from the temperature and humidity when you get to each leg, and altitude
race.li.fuel: Fuelling: carbohydrate, water and sodium per hour, and when to take them
race.li.baiyue: Multi-day Baiyue trips: days split at huts and campsites, pack weight included
race.li.group: Group trips: compare the organiser's timetable with your ability, leg by leg
race.li.share: Save the pacing plan as a session, or share it with your group in one link
race.origin: The formulas for the finish estimate, the environmental corrections and CP are ported from Steve Palladino's SuperPower Calculator (a spreadsheet shared openly in the running-power community) — not our invention; the trail and Baiyue extensions for grade and pack weight follow published literature.
race.shot_alt: The race calculator's legs: grade, pace, power, heart rate and fuelling for each one
plan.h: The schedule and the Season plan
plan.lead: Set your A / B / C races; the season is split into base, build, specific and taper phases, and every week is laid out your way.
plan.li.prefs: Long-run and rest days as you like them; drag a session to another day
plan.li.replan: Finished runs are matched to the plan; replanned when things change, big changes wait for your approval
plan.li.ready: Race readiness: is there time to train, and are you training enough
plan.li.calendar: Subscribe in Google Calendar or the iPhone calendar
plan.shot_alt: The schedule's week view: each day's sessions, their type and whether they were done
read.lead: How your training is going on one page, and every run explained in plain words.
read.li.status: Training load and fatigue trends, this week's volume, days to your next A race
read.li.intervals: How each interval rep went, heart-rate drift, AeT / CP tests recognised automatically
read.li.climb: Climbing speed, whether poles help you, Baiyue achievements, progress on the same climb
read.li.zones: Heart-rate and power zones calibrated on your tests and data
read.shot_alt: The training overview: chronic load, load balance, this week's volume and the training load chart
start.1.p: The first time, you read and accept the terms.
start.2.p: Import FIT files from any watch, or connect intervals.icu; signing in with a COROS or Garmin account is an advanced option (an unofficial interface, at your own risk).
start.3.p: The schedule is built around it, and the calculator can work out that race straight away.
sources.lead: Every calculation cites public literature; the methods and their names belong to their authors. Among them:
sources.list: Banister's training-response model, Tobler's hiking function, the metabolic cost of pack weight, Riegel's distance conversion, Palladino's running power, Joe Friel's heart-rate zones, Uphill Athlete's AeT (aerobic threshold) test, Jack Daniels' return after a break, and the international consensus on heat acclimation.
sources.estimate: A number without a direct source is always marked "estimate" and calibrated on your own data later.
privacy.li.use: Used only to work out your training
privacy.li.export: Download all of it or delete your account at any time
privacy.li.analysis: The de-identified cross-user analysis can be switched off
privacy.li.offline: Add it to your phone's home screen: the schedule opens even without signal in the mountains
faq.watch.q: Which watch do I need? Can I use it without COROS or Garmin?
faq.watch.a: Yes. FIT files from any watch can be imported, and intervals.icu can be connected.
faq.power.q: Can I use it without a Stryd power meter?
faq.power.a: Yes. Without power it uses heart rate: the schedule's targets are heart-rate zones, and power-only charts are hidden.
faq.numbers.q: Why do the numbers differ from my watch?
faq.numbers.a: The two sides compute differently and use different thresholds — that is expected; Settings has a side-by-side of the app's and the watch's values.
faq.estimate.a: A number or rule without a direct source in public literature, estimated from your data or common practice and calibrated on your data later.
faq.data.q: Can I take my data with me?
faq.data.a: Yes. Settings downloads all of it (original FIT files included), and you can delete your account.
end.h: Before your next race, work it out once.
